explanation: CLUTTER is a heap of things lying where they do not belong, which is what "mess" names.
distractor_rationales: "silence" is an absence of sound, not a disorder of objects
KEY
"shortage" is a want of things, the opposite of having too many of them lying about
"delay" is a disorder in time rather than in a space
"stain" is one mark on a surface rather than a scattering of objects

explanation: A potter begins with clay and works it into the finished piece, so the pair is a craftsman and the raw stuff he shapes; "weaver is to yarn" is that same pair.
distractor_rationales: "baker is to oven" gives the equipment the work is done in, not the substance that becomes the loaf
"sculptor is to statue" names the finished work rather than the material it came from
KEY
"tailor is to customer" names the person served rather than anything the tailor works
"carpenter is to workbench" names the surface the work is done on rather than the material worked

explanation: To DRENCH something is to wet it right through, which is to "soak" it.
distractor_rationales: "scatter" spreads things apart rather than wetting one thing through
"polish" works on a surface to brighten it, not to saturate it
"freeze" hardens what is already wet instead of wetting it
"stir" moves a liquid about without putting anything into it
KEY

explanation: A lid is the piece fitted into the mouth of the jar to close it and keep the contents in; "cork is to bottle" is the same closure and the vessel it shuts.
distractor_rationales: KEY
"spout is to kettle" is the part that lets the contents out rather than the part that keeps them in
"label is to can" is a marking stuck on the outside, which closes nothing
"crate is to fruit" is a container and what is put inside it, not a container and its stopper
"shelf is to cupboard" is an interior part of the vessel rather than the thing that seals it

explanation: To VANISH is to pass out of sight altogether, which is to "disappear".
distractor_rationales: "wander" is to move about without a fixed course, and the wanderer remains in view
"tumble" is a manner of falling, which leaves the thing where it can be seen
KEY
"hesitate" is a pause before acting rather than a passing from sight
"gather" brings things together instead of taking them away

explanation: A caterpillar is the earlier form of the very creature that later goes about as a butterfly; "tadpole is to frog" is the same earlier form and the grown animal it becomes.
distractor_rationales: "calf is to herd" sets a young animal beside the group it lives among, not beside its own later self
"cocoon is to silk" sets a case beside the material it is spun from
"fledgling is to nest" sets a young bird beside the place it is raised in
KEY
"swarm is to locust" sets a mass beside one of the creatures composing it

explanation: A STERN teacher allows no easing of the rule, which is to be "strict".
distractor_rationales: KEY
"clumsy" concerns how a person handles things, not how hard a line the person holds
"curious" is an appetite for finding out, which says nothing about severity
"generous" is a readiness to give, and if anything the opposite of holding a hard line
"restless" is an inability to stay still rather than a firmness of temper

explanation: A nest is the shelter a bird makes for itself and lives in; "burrow is to rabbit" is the same dwelling and the animal that dwells in it.
distractor_rationales: "hive is to honey" sets a dwelling beside what is made inside it rather than beside its occupant
"swarm is to bee" sets a mass of creatures beside one of its members
"pasture is to fence" sets a place beside the boundary that encloses it
"saddle is to horse" sets a piece of gear beside the animal it is strapped to
KEY

explanation: To GLEAM is to give off a steady light from a surface, which is to "shine".
distractor_rationales: KEY
"crack" is a splitting of a surface rather than anything it does with light
"float" is a way of resting on water or air
"echo" is a returning of sound rather than of light
"melt" is a change of state brought on by heat, not an appearance of brightness

explanation: Sugar is the substance whose own taste is sweetness; "vinegar is to sour" likewise sets a substance beside the taste that belongs to it.
distractor_rationales: "salt is to preserve" sets a substance beside a use it is put to rather than a taste it has
KEY
"honey is to bee" sets a substance beside the creature that produces it
"pepper is to sneeze" sets a substance beside an effect it causes in a person
"lemon is to fruit" sets a member beside the class it belongs to

explanation: A BLEAK stretch of coast offers nothing to cheer the eye, which is to be "dreary".
distractor_rationales: "hollow" describes a thing empty inside rather than a scene empty of cheer
"narrow" is a measure of width and carries no gloom with it
KEY
"fragile" is a readiness to break, which is a property of an object rather than a mood of a place
"hasty" describes the speed of an action, not the look of a place

explanation: A lullaby is sung for the sake of bringing sleep on, so the pair is an utterance and the response it exists to produce; "joke is to laughter" is that same pair.
distractor_rationales: "sermon is to congregation" sets an utterance beside the people it is addressed to
KEY
"riddle is to answer" sets an utterance beside the reply it demands, which the hearer must supply by work rather than yield up involuntarily
"anthem is to nation" sets a song beside what it honors
"whisper is to secret" sets a manner of speaking beside the sort of thing usually said that way

explanation: An OMINOUS sky is one that gives warning of harm to come, which is to be "threatening".
distractor_rationales: "exhausting" is what wears a person out, not what warns of harm
"bewildering" is what confuses, and a thing may be perfectly clear and still forbode trouble
"flattering" gives pleasure rather than warning
KEY
"refreshing" restores, which is the opposite of what a forbidding sign does

explanation: Rust is the decay that settles on iron and eats the metal away; "mildew is to fabric" is the same decay set beside the material it spoils.
distractor_rationales: "polish is to silver" is a treatment that keeps the metal sound rather than a decay that ruins it
"kiln is to pottery" sets equipment beside the ware fired in it
KEY
"erosion is to wind" names the wearing agent rather than the material worn
"tarnish is to shine" names the quality destroyed rather than the substance attacked

explanation: To COMPILE a list is to gather material from many places and put it together into one, which is to "assemble" it.
distractor_rationales: "memorize" takes material into the mind rather than bringing it together on the page
"translate" carries material from one language into another without adding to it
"abbreviate" cuts material down, the reverse of drawing more of it together
KEY
"distribute" sends material out to many places, the reverse of drawing it in from them

explanation: To pasteurize is to work on milk, the raw stuff that goes in, so that it will keep; "tan is to hide" sets a treatment beside the raw material it is performed on.
distractor_rationales: "churn is to butter" names what comes out of the process rather than the cream that goes in
"grind is to mill" names the machine that performs the work
"brew is to kettle" names the vessel the work is carried out in
"knead is to bread" names the finished loaf rather than the dough that is worked
KEY

explanation: A town that SPRAWLS straggles loosely over more and more ground, which is to "spread out".
distractor_rationales: "settle down" is to come to rest in one place rather than to reach over more of it
"break apart" divides a thing into pieces, whereas what straggles remains one thing
"close in" draws the edges inward, the reverse of reaching outward
KEY
"wear away" loses substance at the edges rather than gaining ground

explanation: The grain is the natural patterning running through the wood itself, which any cut lays bare; "vein is to marble" is the same natural marking within a material.
distractor_rationales: KEY
"knot is to rope" is a feature put in by hand rather than one the material carries of itself
"bark is to tree" is the covering on the outside of a living plant, not a figure running through a material
"resin is to pine" is a substance the tree gives off rather than a marking within its body
"mortar is to brick" is a second material laid between pieces of the first

explanation: An ARDUOUS climb demands sustained hard effort, which is what "laborious" names.
distractor_rationales: "tedious" names the dullness of a task, and a dull task may cost no effort at all
"hazardous" names the danger in a task rather than the labor it costs
"ingenious" praises the cleverness of a contrivance rather than the toil of a job
"spontaneous" describes an act done on the moment's impulse, which says nothing of its difficulty
KEY

explanation: Silt is the matter a river carries along and lays down where it slows, so the pair is a deposit and the moving agent that piled it there; "dune is to wind" is that same pair.
distractor_rationales: KEY
"glacier is to ice" sets a body beside the material it consists of
"wave is to shore" sets a motion beside the place it breaks against
"pebble is to beach" sets a single fragment beside the mass of like fragments it lies among
"crater is to moon" sets a feature beside the body that bears it

explanation: A BRAZEN denial is made in the open with no blush at being caught, which is to be "shameless".
distractor_rationales: "tactless" is a failure to see what will give offense, whereas the bold offender sees it and proceeds
KEY
"reckless" is a disregard of danger rather than of disgrace
"listless" is a want of spirit, the opposite of the effrontery in question
"spotless" is freedom from any fault at all rather than indifference to having one seen

explanation: A curator picks among many works and arranges the chosen few into one exhibition, so the pair is a selector and the made collection that results; "editor is to anthology" is that same pair.
distractor_rationales: "usher is to theater" sets a person beside the building worked in rather than beside anything assembled
"critic is to painting" sets a person beside a single work judged, not beside a collection put together
KEY
"archivist is to records" sets a person beside material kept as it arrives rather than chosen and arranged into a new whole
"patron is to gallery" sets a person beside the institution paid for

explanation: An OSTENTATIOUS display is got up to be admired by onlookers, which is to be "showy".
distractor_rationales: "surly" is ill temper shown to others, whereas what is paraded for admiration is meant to please them
"wasteful" is spending to no purpose, and a great deal may be wasted where nobody is invited to look
"stubborn" is a refusal to be moved, which concerns will rather than display
"talkative" is readiness to speak, and a quiet person may still parade wealth
KEY

explanation: A eulogy is a set piece whose whole business is to praise, so the pair is a form of address and the act it is delivered to perform; "diatribe is to censure" is that same pair.
distractor_rationales: "elegy is to funeral" sets a form beside the occasion it is used at rather than the act it performs
KEY
"sonnet is to rhyme" sets a form beside a device it employs
"satire is to novelist" sets a form beside one sort of person who writes it
"epitaph is to stone" sets a form beside the surface it is cut into

explanation: An INDOLENT heir shrinks from any exertion at all, which is to be "lazy".
distractor_rationales: "greedy" is wanting more than one's share, and the grasping often work hard to get it
"clumsy" is handling things badly, which is a failure of skill rather than of effort
"rude" is roughness toward other people, which has nothing to do with shirking exertion
"stingy" is parting with money unwillingly rather than parting with effort unwillingly
KEY

explanation: To call ground arid is to say that the moisture one might expect in it is simply absent, so the pair is a quality and the thing whose want constitutes it; "insipid is to flavor" is that same pair.
distractor_rationales: KEY
"opaque is to glass" sets a quality beside a material that may happen to have it
"brittle is to snap" sets a quality beside the behavior it invites
"sterile is to clinic" sets a quality beside a place where it is required
"luminous is to lamp" sets a quality beside a thing that possesses it rather than lacks it

explanation: To RESCIND an order is to take it back so that it stands no longer, which is to "repeal" it.
distractor_rationales: "postpone" puts the order off to a later date while leaving it in force
"endorse" gives the order one's backing, the reverse of withdrawing it
"amend" alters the terms of the order but keeps it standing
KEY
"enforce" presses the order upon those bound by it, which presumes it still holds

explanation: A maverick is known by refusing the conformity everyone about him accepts, so the pair is a person and the thing that person is defined by rejecting; "iconoclast is to custom" is that same pair.
distractor_rationales: "hermit is to solitude" names what the person seeks out rather than what the person refuses
KEY
"patriot is to country" names what the person is devoted to
"apprentice is to guild" names a body the person is entering rather than one being defied
"arbiter is to dispute" names what the person is called in to settle

explanation: An INCESSANT hammering goes on without a break from beginning to end, which is what "unceasing" names.
distractor_rationales: "unwelcome" reports how a thing is received, and a welcome noise may run on just as long
"unrivaled" claims that nothing equals the thing, which is a comparison rather than a duration
"unwieldy" describes something awkward to handle because of its bulk
KEY
"unfounded" says a claim rests on nothing, which concerns evidence rather than continuance

explanation: A buttress is raised against a wall for the one purpose of holding it up, so the pair is a support and the thing it keeps standing; "trellis is to vine" is that same pair.
distractor_rationales: "girder is to steel" sets a member beside the metal it is made of
"awning is to shade" sets a structure beside the benefit it affords
KEY
"banister is to staircase" sets a part beside the whole it belongs to rather than a prop beside what it holds up
"quarry is to stone" sets a place beside the material taken out of it
